title: IANUS metadata record (schema version 1.2)
description: Complete IANUS metadata record as it is stored and published. All values set by IANUS are required.
$comment:
Supplement to OPEN-1 of the XSD (naming rule: dot prefix). Decision for the JSON Schema of version 1.2: the keys carry NO prefix. Rule: JSON key = last segment of the XSD name (creator.affiliation.schemeURI -> schemeURI, identifier.ianus -> ianus); xml:lang -> lang. Reasons: (1) The prefix repeats what the nesting of the JSON objects already says. (2) A dot inside a key is read as a path separator by many tools (Elasticsearch, MongoDB, JSONPath- and lodash-style accessors, form libraries); obj["creator.givenName"] instead of obj.givenName. (3) Without the prefix the parts of creator and contributor (name identifier, affiliation) have identical keys and can share code. (4) The keys are equal to the DataCite 4.7 names, so the DataCite export needs no rename step. (5) The prefixed names are long (up to 53 characters). The rule is applied by the generator and checked for collisions; nothing is lost: every node carries its XSD name in x-ianus.xsd_name, so JSON and XML can be converted into each other. The XSD itself keeps the prefix; OPEN-1 stays open for the XSD. Further rules: a container with one repeated child is an array (creators -> array of creator); an element with text and attributes is an object whose text is stored under the element name;
in description is the line break \n. $id is not set because the IANUS domain is not yet fixed. Validators in strict mode must be told the annotation keyword x-ianus (e.g. Ajv: ajv.addKeyword('x-ianus') or strict:false).

publicationYear.title: Year of publication
publicationYear.description: The year when the data was or will be made publicly available. If an embargo period has been in effect, use the date when the embargo period ends. In the case of datasets, “publish” is understood to mean making the data available on a specific date to the community of researchers. If there is no standard publication year value, use the date that would be preferred from a citation perspective. Example: 2026.

geoLocationBox.description: The spatial limits of a box. The box should encompass the area described by geoLocationPlace. documentation.en: The spatial limits of a box. The box should encompass the area described by geoLocationPlace. The box is described by four values, representing the northern, eastern, southern and western boundaries of the geoLocationPlace. Use WGS 84 (World Geodetic System) coordinates and use only decimal numbers for coordinates. For points, enter the identical values for east and west as well as north and south.
documentation.de: The räumlichen Grenzen eines Rechtecks, das die durch den geoLocationPoint bezeichneten Raum umschließt. Das Rechteck wird durch die vier Werte für die nördliche, östliche, südliche und westliche Grenze des Bereichs beschrieben. Es ist WGS 84 (World Geodetic System) für die Angabe der Koordinaten zu verwenden und diese sind als Dezimalzahlen einzugeben (Dezimalgrad-Angaben). Zur Angabe von Punktkoordianten einfach die identischen Werte bei Ost und West bzw. Nord und Süd eingeben.
